<p class="cycle-role">Existing knowledge and its relevance across places.</p>

<p class="page-deck"><strong>How does place shape which urban climate knowledge is produced, recognised and useful elsewhere?</strong></p>

We study how urban climate knowledge is distributed across places, which cities can plausibly learn from one another, and how institutional and geographic context shapes the relevance of evidence produced elsewhere.

::: {.notice}
**Part of a connected learning cycle.** Projects and cities may enter at different points. Evidence about consequences can revise judgements about existing knowledge and where new evidence matters.
:::

## Questions the lab investigates

- Where is urban climate knowledge produced, recognised and made visible?
- Which cities can plausibly learn from one another, and under what conditions?
- How do institutional and geographic contexts shape replication, comparison and case-study usefulness?

## Analytical boundary

- Claims that evidence transfers intact or applies unchanged between cities.
- Simple inventories of policy adoption that do not examine evidence, comparison or learning.
